newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says imported sugar swamps market.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says imported sugar swamps market.

text.p: Philippine Sugar Regulatory Administration head Wilson Gamboa said on Friday he had ordered traders and millers to import no more sugar for the next six months because of a glut.
Gamboa said the Philippines imported 1.23 million tonnes of sugar from neighbouring countries from September 1995 to July 1996, resulting in an excess of 423,000 tonnes.
Local sugar traders imported sugar in the last crop year ending August due to a local production shortfall.
But Gamboa said there was over-importation of 423,000 tonnes.
"We (have) sugar up to our ears," Gamboa told reporters.
Local sugar prices dropped to a low of 525 pesos per 50 kg bag two weeks ago from a high of 800 pesos last year because of the imported sugar, Gamboa said.
Sugar prices from local mills, however, seem to be recovering with the average price reaching 671 pesos per 50 kg bag, he added.
Gamboa said his agency had ordered the export to the United States of 78,000 tonnes of locally grown sugar from October to December this year to lessen the country's sugar stock.
Sugar planters and traders were also asked to ship to the United States "at the earliest possible time," some 53,000 tonnes, which had been scheduled for delivery between January to March 1997.
The Philippines is one of the beneficiaries of a programme under which developing nations export sugar to the United States at premium prices.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture announced last month it has cut the raw cane sugar allocation for the Philippines by 8.4 percent to 219,059 tonnes for crop year 1996/1997 from the previous 237,422 tonnes.
